506	Let us mention in this context an idea that is simple,
507	wonderful, sublime, an idea that fills the heart with strength,
508	that truly gives something to hold on to in these last moments
509	of the exile.
510	The custom of the Sephardim, the custom of the Eastern communities,
511	is to begin the Kinot on the night of Tisha beAv with the kinah
512	of Haazinu.
513	Yes, even before the other Kinot, they begin
514	to read the kinah of Haazinu, the terrible prophecies of destruction
515	that Moshe Rabbeinu spoke. The kinah of Haazinu foretells
516	bad days, hard days that even the greatest prophets of the destruction
517	did not expect the like of. Moshe Rabbeinu says verses
518	that are hard even to repeat. He quotes
519	the Holy One, blessed be He: I said, days will come when the Holy One,
520	blessed be He, will say, "I would scatter them to the corners,"
521	I will throw them away like the corner of the field. I will cast the people of
522	Israel to the corners of the world, one Jew here, one Jew
523	there, so that they lose all meaning. Grain
524	that is concentrated, that is gathered, has importance, has
525	weight, has volume, has meaning. But
526	when you throw one stalk here and one stalk
527	there, and one kernel here and one kernel there, it has
528	no force, no meaning, no
529	weight. "I would scatter them to the corners": I will cast the people of Israel
530	into the corners of the world like merchandise nobody wants, like
531	merchandise nobody desires. And He goes on and says terrible words:
532	"I would make their memory cease from among men."
533	Days will come when the Holy One, blessed be He, will want to destroy
534	the people of Israel, not only the body, heaven forbid, but
535	the memory of the people of Israel, so that no one will remember that there once was
536	a people of Israel. The destruction will be so total, acute,
537	and terrible that no one will remember that there was once such a phenomenon
538	called the chosen people of the Holy One, blessed be He.
539	And why will He not do it? Why are we here
540	today, thank HaShem, alive and kicking? "Were it not that I feared the enemy's
541	provocation, lest their adversaries misjudge": only so that the enemy does not
542	win.
543	"I will not destroy the people of Israel, only so as not to let
544	Hitler" win. Let us imagine to what lowliness the people of
545	Israel would sink, that the people of Israel would remain alive in the world: a Father
546	would leave the son alive in the world not because the son deserves
547	mercy, but only so that the enemy does not take victory.
548	Let us imagine terrible and dreadful things. There are no other
549	prophecies as hard and terrible as the kinah of
550	Haazinu. And here one question arises: so why is it a song?
551	Why is Haazinu a song and not a kinah? On the night of Tisha beAv
552	the Eastern communities read it as a kinah,
553	but all year it is a song. First, in the Torah itself it
554	is written in verse form. Second, it is written like two
555	columns with a break in the middle, the way a song is written. Third,
556	in the Beit HaMikdash the Levites would sing it, literally
557	with song and melody. Every Shabbat they would sing "HaZiv Lach."
558	"HaZiv Lach" means they would divide the song of Haazinu
559	into six parts, and every Shabbat they would sing one part.
560	Accordingly, in the synagogue we divide
561	the first part of Haazinu into six aliyot. "HaZiv Lach":
562	"Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; remember the days of old," we divide
563	the song of Haazinu into six
564	parts
565	and we read the first six aliyot the way
566	the Levites would sing in the Beit HaMikdash. They sing for six Shabbatot
567	and then it starts again from the beginning. How can one
568	picture what the Levites sang? "I would scatter them,"
569	"I would make their memory cease": to what melody did they sing it? We are talking
570	about terrible prophecies of exile, which one should read
571	sitting on the ground, on Tisha beAv night,
572	and the Levites would sing suffering, sing pain. An
573	enormous question lies here: is Haazinu a song, or is Haazinu
574	a kinah? How can we understand the whole matter?
575	The Rebbe once said something truly brilliant in Likutei Sichot,
576	in a short note he said it, but it is truly something
577	so special:
578	Haazinu is a song because it films the entire path.
579	Haazinu is a song because it is a panoramic picture
580	of all the chapters, all the chapters in the life of the people of
581	Israel. Haazinu, says the Ramban, depicts past, present,
582	and future. In the song of Haazinu, the suffering, the pain, the
583	terrible kinah is a chapter
584	within the great plan that leads to the redemption.
585	And over this a Jew sings: not over this moment, but over the understanding
586	that this moment produces redemption, produces good,
587	produces a greatness that the good days did not produce.
588	A Jew does not sing over this moment as it is, but over
589	this moment as it is part of the movement of the train, part
590	of the progress of the ship,
591	of the progress of the route, part of the trouble
592	that becomes a skylight and builds the future redemption. Let us
593	see: here He began with the past, "He found him in a desert land,"
594	"He encircled him, He cared for him, as an eagle stirs up its nest, over its young
595	it hovers." The days after the Exodus from Egypt, the giving of the Torah:
596	the Holy One, blessed be He, carried us like an eagle on the
597	wings, we were at the height of the world, at the peak of the world.
598	And then comes the descent, comes the terrible exile.
